chunks: And in another Hadith of Abdul Rahman,

he said, 'I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and he had massaged with flour mixed with oil. So I said to him, 'The people are disliking that'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it'.

key_terms.تَدَلَّكَ: to massage or rub the body
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use flour mixed with oil for massage during ritual bathing in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) addresses the ritual purity of using flour mixed with oil for massage in the bathhouse. When asked about the people's dislike for this practice, the Imam confirmed its permissibility, indicating that such substances do not invalidate ritual purity. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between mere physical presence of a substance and the actual barrier it forms to water, emphasizing that thin layers of oil and flour do not prevent water from reaching the skin during ablution or full-body washing.

en.hubeali: And in another Hadeeth of Abdul Rahman,

he said, 
‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and he had massaged with flour mixed with oil. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The people are disliking that’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: Afi ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘ Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajj aj who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who applies lime, then mixes flour with oil then rubs it on him after lime to remove its smell. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
